newsitem.title: UK: UK's Major sends congratulations to Clinton.
newsitem.headline: UK's Major sends congratulations to Clinton.

text.p: British Prime Minister John Major said on Wednesday that U.S. President Bill Clinton had received a resounding vote of confidence from the American people.
Major's office said he had sent a personal message of congratulations to Clinton on winning a second term in the White House and would to speak to him by telephone at the start of the U.S day.
"The prime minister warmly congratulates the president on his re-election. He has won a resounding vote of confidence from the American people," said an official statement.

"The president has campaigned on his record and his economic and political achievements have spoken for themselves. The prime minister looks forward to continuing to work closely with the president over the next four years."
Opposition Labour leader Tony Blair, who is hoping to oust Major's Conservatives in elections which must be held within the next nine months, said he was "absolutely delighted" for Clinton.

"This is a great victory and a personal triumph for the president," Blair said, adding: "He has shown the way that the tide of ideas is turning against the extremes of the right and in favour of progressive politics."

Liberal Democrat leader Paddy Ashdown said: "Bill Clinton's victory is a triumph for progressive politics over conservatism and reaction. The biggest lesson for Britain is that a campaign that is more about style than substance is a turn-off for voters."
